Directive DIRECTIVE_045: PRs-Only and Read-Intent Before High-Risk Operations
    Intent: All changes to the remote main branch go through pull requests — agents never push directly or merge without explicit operator instruction. Before executing any high-risk git operation (merge, rebase, deletion, force operations), agents must read the mission spec and current context first. Neither rule may be bypassed under time pressure or assumed from a task title alone.
    Scope: Applies to all agent-driven git operations that touch the remote main branch (origin/main) or that constitute high-risk operations: merges, rebases, deletions of branches or files, and force operations. Also applies during any review or implementation step that could result in one of these operations.
    Procedures:
      - All changes to origin/main must go through pull requests; never run `git push origin main` or `gh pr merge` without explicit operator instruction. The operator always merges to origin/main manually.
      - After `spec-kitty merge` (which merges to local main only and does NOT push to origin/main), create a PR branch (`git checkout -b pr/<slug>`) and open a pull request (`gh pr create`). Do not push to origin/main directly.
      - Recovery if origin/main is accidentally pushed to — do NOT force-push (branch protection blocks it). Create a `revert/<slug>` branch from origin/main, commit a revert, open a PR to merge it, then open the real mission PR.
      - Before executing any high-risk git operation (merge, rebase, deletion of branches or files, force operations), read the mission spec and the current context first. Never execute from a task title or a one-line description alone.
      - If the intent of a high-risk operation is unclear or the context is insufficient, escalate to the operator rather than proceeding. Correctness takes precedence over speed.
      - Never delete a test to make a build pass; such a deletion is a high-risk operation that requires explicit intent confirmation.
    Integrity rules:
      - Agents must not run `git push origin main`, `git push --force`, or `gh pr merge` without explicit operator instruction.
      - `spec-kitty merge` is permitted — it operates on local main only. The prohibition applies to pushing the result to origin/main without a PR.
      - Every high-risk git operation must be preceded by a documented intent check (reading mission spec/context). "The task title said to do it" is not sufficient justification.
      - PR branches and mission branches are the correct terms for non-main branches in canonical voice. The colloquial "feature branch" is a git idiom that must be quoted and marked when it appears in examples; it must not appear unquoted in canonical agent instructions.
    Validation criteria:
      - Agent guidance for merge operations explicitly states that `spec-kitty merge` targets local main only and that a PR branch must be opened before the result reaches origin/main.
      - High-risk operation checklists require a mission-spec/context read step before execution.
      - No agent workflow example uses `git push origin main` or `gh pr merge` without explicit operator-authorization language.
      - Escalation path (to the operator) is documented for cases where intent is unclear.
